explanation_en: This is a highly common discourse marker meaning 'in fact' or 'as a matter of fact.' It is used to introduce a statement that confirms, details, or provides evidence for a previous point. It is essential for B2/C1 learners to connect ideas smoothly in conversation.

examples.en_text: I don't think it's going to rain today; in fact, the sky is completely clear.
examples.target_text: No creo que vaya a llover hoy; de hecho, el cielo está completamente despejado.

examples.en_text: I know Laura very well; in fact, we went to the same school when we were kids.
examples.target_text: Conozco muy bien a Laura; de hecho, fuimos a la misma escuela cuando éramos niños.

examples.en_text: The new employee learns very quickly; in fact, he already knows how to use the whole system.
examples.target_text: El nuevo empleado aprende muy rápido; de hecho, ya sabe usar todo el sistema.

examples.en_text: I love spicy food; in fact, I always put extra sauce on my dishes.
examples.target_text: Me encanta la comida picante; de hecho, siempre le pongo salsa extra a mis platos.

examples.en_text: We were thinking of going out this weekend, but in fact we prefer to stay home and rest.
examples.target_text: Pensábamos salir este fin de semana, pero de hecho preferimos quedarnos en casa a descansar.

examples.en_text: This book is not as difficult as it seems; in fact, I've already read three chapters today.
examples.target_text: Este libro no es tan difícil como parece; de hecho, ya he leído tres capítulos hoy.

explanation_en: This expression is used to indicate that something exceeds the limits, scope, or importance of a specific thing. It is very common in both written and spoken Spanish to elevate the significance of an event or concept. Learners should note that it is followed by the preposition 'de'.

examples.en_text: Our friendship goes beyond work; we are like brothers.
examples.target_text: Nuestra amistad va más allá del trabajo; somos como hermanos.

examples.en_text: To learn a language, you have to go beyond grammar rules.
examples.target_text: Para aprender un idioma, hay que ir más allá de las reglas gramaticales.

examples.en_text: The company always tries to go beyond customer expectations.
examples.target_text: La empresa siempre intenta ir más allá de las expectativas de los clientes.

examples.en_text: Sometimes we need to go beyond our comfort zone to grow.
examples.target_text: A veces necesitamos ir más allá de nuestra zona de confort para crecer.

examples.en_text: You have to go beyond his words to understand what he really feels.
examples.target_text: Tienes que ir más allá de sus palabras para entender lo que realmente siente.

examples.en_text: This project goes beyond a simple school task; it is a real investigation.
examples.target_text: Este proyecto va más allá de una simple tarea escolar; es una investigación real.

explanation_en: A very common filler and emphatic phrase meaning 'of course' or 'certainly'. It is used to reinforce an assertion. It is highly natural in conversational and journalistic Spanish, serving as a synonym for 'por supuesto' or 'sin duda'.

examples.en_text: Without a doubt, this is the best decision we have made this year.
examples.target_text: Desde luego, esta es la mejor decisión que hemos tomado este año.

examples.en_text: —'Can you help me prepare dinner?' —'Of course, tell me what to do.'
examples.target_text: —¿Me puedes ayudar a preparar la cena? —Desde luego, dime qué hago.

examples.en_text: The driving test was difficult, but it was certainly worth studying so much.
examples.target_text: El examen de conducir fue difícil, pero desde luego valió la pena estudiar tanto.

examples.en_text: Of course, we will send you the detailed budget by email first thing tomorrow.
examples.target_text: Desde luego, le enviaremos el presupuesto detallado por correo electrónico mañana mismo.

examples.en_text: I don't know who will win the match, but they certainly played much better today.
examples.target_text: No sé quién ganará el partido, pero desde luego ellos han jugado mucho mejor hoy.

examples.en_text: Of course I am not going to accept that job if the salary is so low.
examples.target_text: Desde luego que no voy a aceptar ese trabajo si el sueldo es tan bajo.

explanation_en: This collocation means to make a significant impact over a long period, essentially defining a generation or era. It is commonly used in sports, arts, and history. It implies leaving a lasting legacy.

examples.en_text: That rock band defined an era in the nineties.
examples.target_text: Esa banda de rock marcó una época en los años noventa.

examples.en_text: The launch of the first smartphone has defined an era.
examples.target_text: El lanzamiento del primer teléfono inteligente ha marcado una época.

examples.en_text: With his talent, this young tennis player is ready to make history.
examples.target_text: Con su talento, este joven tenista está listo para marcar una época.

examples.en_text: Her fashion designs defined an era and changed the way people dressed.
examples.target_text: Sus diseños de moda marcaron una época y cambiaron la forma de vestir de la gente.

examples.en_text: There are movies that not only entertain, but also define an era.
examples.target_text: Hay películas que no solo entretienen, sino que marcan una época.

examples.en_text: We want to create an innovative product that defines an era in the industry.
examples.target_text: Queremos crear un producto innovador que marque una época en la industria.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means to do something immediately after an event occurs, while emotions are still high or the situation is still fresh, without much reflection. It contrasts with 'en frío' (with a cool head / after some time has passed). It is highly colloquial but widely used in journalism and everyday speech.

examples.en_text: It's better not to make important decisions in the heat of the moment; wait until you are calmer.
examples.target_text: Es mejor no tomar decisiones importantes en caliente; espera a estar más tranquilo.

examples.en_text: I prefer to write the meeting notes while they are fresh so I don't forget any details.
examples.target_text: Prefiero escribir las notas de la reunión en caliente para no olvidar ningún detalle.

examples.en_text: I told him I wanted to break up in the heat of the moment, but now I regret my words.
examples.target_text: Le dije que quería romper en caliente, pero ahora me arrepiento de mis palabras.

examples.en_text: The coach gave us his feedback right away, right after finishing the game.
examples.target_text: El entrenador nos dio su opinión en caliente, justo después de terminar el partido.

examples.en_text: In the heat of the moment I didn't feel the blow to my ankle, but the next day I couldn't walk.
examples.target_text: En caliente no sentí el golpe en el tobillo, pero al día siguiente no podía caminar.

examples.en_text: We must take advantage of the inspiration and finish composing the song while it's fresh.
examples.target_text: Debemos aprovechar la inspiración y terminar de componer la canción en caliente.

explanation_en: This phrase literally means 'halfway between' but is frequently used metaphorically to describe a state, feeling, or situation that is a blend of two different things. It is a great way to express nuance and compromise between two concepts.

examples.en_text: The hotel is halfway between the beach and the city center.
examples.target_text: El hotel está a mitad de camino entre la playa y el centro de la ciudad.

examples.en_text: His dressing style is halfway between classic and modern.
examples.target_text: Su estilo de vestir está a mitad de camino entre lo clásico y lo moderno.

examples.en_text: We stopped at a gas station halfway between Madrid and Valencia.
examples.target_text: Paramos en una gasolinera a mitad de camino entre Madrid y Valencia.

examples.en_text: The taste of this fruit is halfway between an apple and a pear.
examples.target_text: El sabor de esta fruta está a mitad de camino entre una manzana y una pera.

examples.en_text: My house is halfway between the train station and the office.
examples.target_text: Mi casa queda a mitad de camino entre la estación de tren y la oficina.

examples.en_text: The movie is halfway between a comedy and a drama.
examples.target_text: La película está a mitad de camino entre una comedia y un drama.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to put on one's overalls', this idiom is widely used in Spain to describe the act of preparing for hard, gritty, or unglamorous work. In sports, it refers to defending hard and fighting for every ball rather than just playing beautifully. It is highly idiomatic and common in everyday discussions about work, projects, or sports.

examples.en_text: If we want to finish the project on time, we have to roll up our sleeves starting today.
examples.target_text: Si queremos terminar el proyecto a tiempo, tenemos que ponernos el mono de trabajo desde hoy.

examples.en_text: After the holidays, it was hard for me to get down to work and start studying again.
examples.target_text: Después de las vacaciones, me costó ponerme el mono de trabajo y volver a estudiar.

examples.en_text: The rival team is very strong, so today we have to roll up our sleeves to win.
examples.target_text: El equipo rival es muy fuerte, así que hoy toca ponerse el mono de trabajo para ganar.

examples.en_text: We have to paint the whole house this weekend, so let's roll up our sleeves!
examples.target_text: Hay que pintar toda la casa este fin de semana, así que ¡a ponerse el mono de trabajo!

examples.en_text: The employees rolled up their sleeves and managed to save the company from the crisis.
examples.target_text: Los empleados se pusieron el mono de trabajo y lograron salvar la empresa de la crisis.

examples.en_text: Stop complaining, roll up your sleeves, and help your brother clean the garden.
examples.target_text: Deja de quejarte, ponte el mono de trabajo y ayuda a tu hermano a limpiar el jardín.

explanation_en: This expression means to engage in a tough, gritty, or even dirty fight or struggle, leaving aside elegance or high principles to do what is necessary to win. It is common in politics, sports, and business. It implies facing a difficult, messy situation head-on.

examples.en_text: The candidate got down in the mud in the last election debate to attack his rival.
examples.target_text: El candidato bajó al barro en el último debate electoral para atacar a su rival.

examples.en_text: A good boss doesn't just give orders; they also have to get their hands dirty when the team needs it.
examples.target_text: Un buen jefe no solo da órdenes, también tiene que bajar al barro cuando el equipo lo necesita.

examples.en_text: I know you're angry, but don't stoop to their level by responding to their insults.
examples.target_text: Sé que estás enfadado, pero no bajes al barro contestando a sus insultos.

examples.en_text: If we want to win this match, we have to roll up our sleeves and fight for every ball.
examples.target_text: Si queremos ganar este partido, tenemos que bajar al barro y luchar por cada balón.

examples.en_text: After months of theoretical planning, it's finally time to get down to the real work and start the project.
examples.target_text: Después de meses de planificación teórica, por fin es hora de bajar al barro y empezar el trabajo real.

examples.en_text: That journalist is not afraid to get his hands dirty to uncover the truth about corruption.
examples.target_text: A ese periodista no le da miedo bajar al barro para descubrir la verdad sobre la corrupción.

explanation_en: This idiom means to express something very clearly, leaving no room for doubt. When applied to facts or statistics, it means they provide unmistakable evidence of a situation. It is a more sophisticated alternative to 'hablar claro' or 'demostrar claramente'.

examples.en_text: I think it's time to speak openly and resolve this misunderstanding once and for all.
examples.target_text: Creo que es hora de hablar a las claras y resolver este malentendido de una vez por todas.

examples.en_text: The director spoke frankly about the company's financial problems during the meeting.
examples.target_text: El director habló a las claras sobre los problemas financieros de la empresa durante la reunión.

examples.en_text: The exam results speak clearly of your effort this semester.
examples.target_text: Los resultados del examen hablan a las claras de tu esfuerzo este semestre.

examples.en_text: If you want the relationship to work, you have to speak openly to your partner.
examples.target_text: Si quieres que la relación funcione, tienes que hablarle a las claras a tu pareja.

examples.en_text: Citizens appreciate when a politician speaks frankly and doesn't hide the truth.
examples.target_text: Los ciudadanos agradecen cuando un político habla a las claras y no esconde la verdad.

examples.en_text: I always prefer people to speak frankly to me, even if the truth is painful.
examples.target_text: Siempre prefiero que me hablen a las claras, aunque la verdad sea dolorosa.

explanation_en: This common phrase means to accept defeat gracefully and with sportsmanship, without complaining, making excuses, or acting bitter. Its counterpart is 'saber ganar' (to be a gracious winner). It is widely used in sports, games, and life in general.

examples.en_text: In sports, it is as important to win as it is to know how to lose.
examples.target_text: En el deporte, es tan importante ganar como saber perder.

examples.en_text: My younger brother never knows how to lose; he always gets angry when we play cards.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano menor nunca sabe perder; siempre se enfada cuando jugamos a las cartas.

examples.en_text: If you want to be a good leader, you have to learn to be a good loser with dignity.
examples.target_text: Si quieres ser un buen líder, tienes que aprender a saber perder con dignidad.

examples.en_text: I like playing with them because they are honest and know how to be good losers.
examples.target_text: Me gusta jugar con ellos porque son honestos y saben perder.

examples.en_text: The candidate accepted the election results and showed that he knows how to be a good loser.
examples.target_text: El candidato aceptó los resultados de las elecciones y demostró que sabe perder.

examples.en_text: Don't worry about the result of the match, the important thing is that you know how to lose.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes por el resultado del partido, lo importante es que sepas perder.

explanation_en: Though the speaker adds an extra 'en' here by mistake, 'de manera conjunta' is a very common adverbial locution meaning 'together' or 'jointly.' It is preferred in formal, academic, or professional settings over 'juntos.' It collocates frequently with verbs like 'trabajar,' 'desarrollar,' and 'abordar.'

examples.en_text: Both departments must work jointly to finish the project on time.
examples.target_text: Ambos departamentos deben trabajar de manera conjunta para terminar el proyecto a tiempo.

examples.en_text: My parents made the decision jointly after talking about it a lot.
examples.target_text: Mis padres tomaron la decisión de manera conjunta después de hablarlo mucho.

examples.en_text: The neighbors decided to clean the park together this weekend.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos decidieron limpiar el parque de manera conjunta este fin de semana.

examples.en_text: The two universities are researching climate change jointly.
examples.target_text: Las dos universidades están investigando el cambio climático de manera conjunta.

examples.en_text: The governments of both countries issued a statement jointly.
examples.target_text: Los gobiernos de ambos países emitieron un comunicado de manera conjunta.

examples.en_text: We are organizing the birthday party together to share the expenses.
examples.target_text: Estamos organizando la fiesta de cumpleaños de manera conjunta para compartir los gastos.

explanation_en: In this context, 'sentido' refers to direction (e.g., 'sentido único' means 'one-way'). 'Poner el sentido de' is used here to describe establishing the flow or direction of traffic. Learners should be careful not to confuse 'sentido' (direction) with 'sentido' (feeling or sense).

examples.en_text: It is important to set the direction of the baby seat facing backwards for safety.
examples.target_text: Es importante poner el sentido de la silla del bebé en contra de la marcha por seguridad.

examples.en_text: The city council is going to set the direction of this street towards the center to avoid traffic jams.
examples.target_text: El ayuntamiento va a poner el sentido de esta calle hacia el centro para evitar atascos.

examples.en_text: Before starting the car, remember to set the direction of the navigation on the map.
examples.target_text: Antes de arrancar el coche, recuerda poner el sentido de la navegación en el mapa.

examples.en_text: Can we set the direction of the train seats forward so we don't get dizzy?
examples.target_text: ¿Podemos poner el sentido de los asientos del tren hacia adelante para no marearnos?

examples.en_text: For the machine to work well, you must set the direction of the belt to the left.
examples.target_text: Para que la máquina funcione bien, debes poner el sentido de la cinta hacia la izquierda.

examples.en_text: The company's new plan seeks to set the direction of the brand towards a younger audience.
examples.target_text: El nuevo plan de la empresa busca poner el sentido de la marca hacia un público más joven.
